variants.direction: Make an elegant but rugged streamlined central hull with a decisive two-level side profile. A long upper shoulder shelf steps inward toward the clear central baydoors; below it one deep horizontal recess runs from behind the collar to the wing root. The original fan-wing root sits in a thick faceted recessed saddle. Three broad fan leaves have different lengths, crisp clipped tips and one broad inset sector on each, so deployed wings read as layered architectural planes. Integrate the collar into the shoulders with short tapered transitions without enlarging it. The aft engine housings repeat the body's two stepped levels, with wide flat sides and a compact solid crosswise equipment pad. Large areas stay calm; depth, silhouette breaks and functional replacements provide pirate character. Avoid simply adding plates over the original rectangular body.
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Design an upgraded LI PIR ELITE pirate heavy fighter from Freelancer (2003). Make a coherent industrial Liberty Art Deco ship redesign, using these specific game references rather than generic science-fiction styling.

REFERENCE AUTHORITY: Images 1 and 2 show the exact ORIGINAL CABIN, with four views, textured and neutral. Its geometry, glazing boundaries, frames, dimensions and mounting are immutable. Image 3 is the complete current pirate ship in actual DEPLOYED FLIGHT pose, including true top/side/front and clay shape. Image 4 is its historical Liberty Mercenary Elite Fighter concept art: borrow its elegant streamlined body, stepped transverse collar and folding fan vocabulary, but do NOT copy its DIFFERENT short arched cabin, white military finish or insignia. Image 5 shows the actual three linked fan-wing leaves per side folding together; use this for mechanical topology and deployed shape.

COMPOSITION: ONE ship design only, a landscape production concept sheet on pale warm neutral paper. Large front three-quarter perspective, nose pointing LEFT, showing the whole ship with generous margins. Below it, a clean SIDE PROFILE and a clean TOP VIEW of this SAME ship in DEPLOYED flight. Consistent proportions, no alternate designs mixed in. Header as specified below; labels only SIDE and TOP. Detailed painted game concept finish, crisply readable volumes, soft studio light, no space battle, weapons or scenery. Medium-rich geometric detail like a practical modeller's concept, not microdetail noise.

IMMUTABLE CABIN: Visually transplant the actual cabin from images 1/2. It is an elongated low rounded capsule at the very FRONT, not a little canopy sitting on the top of a long pointed nose. Its glazed nose is blunt and faceted-round, with a long broad central roof pane, large curved side panes, small rear side panes, lower front glazing and the original narrow structural divisions. Copy the actual native pane shapes and surrounding shell, including the short neck and seat immediately ahead of the stepped collar. Do not reshape it into a fighter-jet canopy, a BW angular windshield, a truck window or the short high arch of image 4. Do not add a long beak ahead of it. Keep cabin width, length and physical scale relative to image 3, in all three views. If the new body conflicts with the cabin, adjust the body, never the cabin. Do not turn tiny source hardpoint pads into glazing or new cabin fittings.

IDENTITY AND STRUCTURE: Preserve the compact long central fuselage, original front capsule, narrow neck with THREE transverse stepped collar flanges, two side wings made of THREE broad interleaving SOLID FAN LEAVES each, and two aft-facing engines stacked CLOSE TOGETHER at the rear of the same body. The upper exhaust is larger; the second is below it. This is not a BW keel ship and not a Rheinland drum design. Original deployed body envelope about width 13.92, height 5.97, length 15.05: keep that broad compact fighter scale. Fan roots are tilted downward about 22.5 degrees; the wings fan outward in their inclined plane. Three chained leaves have 20-degree hinge offsets each when deployed; they nest inward/back against one another for docking. Show three connected overlapping leaves per side, not nine thin fins, not feathers, not an exposed umbrella rib cage. Enclose hubs in broad functional root sockets and leave visible separation seams for movement. Preserve pointed clipped sector tips.

BAYDOOR AND TAIL: There are TWO long closed cargo doors along the top of the central fuselage behind the neck, opening outward/up. Leave the center seam and outer hinge line clear; no fixed ornamental bridge, raised spine or strip crossing the door sweep. The two rear engines and a compact transverse upper rear equipment platform remain integrated with the body. Keep tail robust and compact; no large exposed outer frame or tall rear wing.

LIBERTY ART DECO: Express the style in the SHAPE: stepped setbacks, long parallel speed lines, broad sunburst/fan sectors, nested trapezoids, restrained concentric collar steps and solid rounded-to-faceted transitions. Contrast the native rounded cabin with crisp geometric shoulders. Rhythm comes from a FEW purposeful volumes, recessed panels and deep shadow slots. Avoid golden filigree, decorative skyscrapers, raygun toys, ornamental gold borders, jewelry, excessive ribs and surface-only motifs. A Liberty ship built and repaired by pirates, still a fast heavy fighter.

PIRATE REWORK: Make the silhouette and medium-scale structure meaningfully different from image 3 while retaining the listed identity. Integrate a few mismatched replacement hull sections and heavy contained joints into the architecture, with asymmetric repair seams but a balanced flight silhouette. Muted weathered oxide-red/brown native hull, some dull worn light-metal repair areas, charcoal inset grilles, blue-grey native glazing. Keep wear controlled so the shape reads. No skulls, demons, spikes, flags, exposed piping, wire bundles, external scaffolding or geometric rivets. Do not add repeated tiny plating or greeble mountains. No transport bulk, no capital-ship scale.

DIRECTION:
Make an elegant but rugged streamlined central hull with a decisive two-level side profile. A long upper shoulder shelf steps inward toward the clear central baydoors; below it one deep horizontal recess runs from behind the collar to the wing root. The original fan-wing root sits in a thick faceted recessed saddle. Three broad fan leaves have different lengths, crisp clipped tips and one broad inset sector on each, so deployed wings read as layered architectural planes. Integrate the collar into the shoulders with short tapered transitions without enlarging it. The aft engine housings repeat the body's two stepped levels, with wide flat sides and a compact solid crosswise equipment pad. Large areas stay calm; depth, silhouette breaks and functional replacements provide pirate character. Avoid simply adding plates over the original rectangular body.

Header text exactly: "LI PIR ELITE — L01". Produce one coherent three-view ship sheet, with the original capsule cabin unmistakably preserved.

variants.direction: Make a more distinctive raider silhouette through angular CUT-IN shapes. Each hull flank has one deep backward-pointing chevron-shaped recess with solid sloped walls; the recess flows into a compact broad root socket where the three fan leaves overlap. Put a single stepped diagonal break in the shoulder outline, echoing the fan's converging lines. Keep the central top baydoors unobstructed and preserve the original front capsule and three collar steps. Fan sectors use bold trapezoidal tip cuts and deep inset fields, with continuous solid leading load paths, no open rod frameworks. The aft housing is a tapered octagonal block split into two engine terraces, with a low crosswise equipment shelf. Industrial repairs are visible as two or three integrated mismatched sections. The chevrons and nested sectors must read in silhouette and shadow, without turning into ornamental surface graphics.
